OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'

## What I did

The spec required rejecting owner creation when any of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, or `telephone` is missing or blank, responding `400` with a JSON body whose `errors` array names each offending field.

I added a **single new, self-contained file** — `OwnerFieldsValidationAdvice.java` — and touched no existing method:

- It extends `RequestBodyAdviceAdapter` and validates the `OwnerFieldsDto` right after the request body is deserialized (before the controller runs), collecting the names of any null/blank required fields via a small `isBlank` check (which also catches the `"   "` whitespace-only telephone case).
- If any are missing it throws a nested `MissingOwnerFieldsException` carrying the field list, and a co-located `@ExceptionHandler` returns `400` with `{"errors":[...]}`.
- `@Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)` ensures this advice is consulted before the existing generic `ExceptionControllerAdvice` (whose broad `Exception` handler would otherwise turn it into a 500); for any other exception this advice has no matching handler, so it cleanly falls through to the existing one.

## Why this keeps structural impact low

The cost model punishes editing methods inside large classes (`WMC_other` pays for the whole class) and multiplies by files touched. I therefore:
- **Touched zero existing methods** — no edit to the busy `OwnerRestControllerV1` or to `ExceptionControllerAdvice`, both high-`WMC_other` classes.
- **Added one cohesive file** with tiny methods (each CC ≈ 1, so `WMC_other` within the new class is minimal), keeping the whole change to a single small unit.
